title: Soft steamed broccoli trees
summary: Big, soft broccoli florets with a built-in handle: an easy first finger food for little fists.
texture: Very soft: the head should squash flat when you press it between your thumb and finger. Leave a long stalk as a handle.
ingredients: 1 small head broccoli, cut into large florets with long stalks
1 tsp olive oil or a little unsalted butter (optional)
steps: Steam the florets for 7 to 10 minutes, until very tender and easily pierced through the stalk.
Test one: press the head between your thumb and finger. If it doesn't squash easily, steam a few minutes more.
Toss with a little olive oil or melted butter if you like, then cool before serving.
choking: Serve large florets, not small pieces: a long stalk is easier for baby to hold and gnaw.
Undercooked broccoli is too firm. It must squash easily.

allergens.name: Milk (if using butter)
allergens.note: Leave out the butter or use olive oil if your baby hasn't had dairy yet.

storage: Fridge up to 2 days. Reheat by steaming briefly, then cool. Freezing makes them soggy but fine for mashing.
tips: Cauliflower and green beans (very soft, whole) work the same way.
Expect some broccoli to end up everywhere but baby's mouth. Playing with food is part of learning.
